Nothing sits in the x32 lane, which runs clear from the door at x31 z11 to the stove. Two hanging lanterns at y6 (x32 z12, x33 z14) light every floor cell at 10 or more; no dark cells.
make.sh ran whole (saved 3152 cells); this part placed 12 blocks with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE writes; room check FIT OK, 0 dark. The walk verdict says unreachable only because the front door and stair hall are not built yet.
left: Walk verdict is UNREACHABLE from the entrance because the front door x29 z9 (fittings) and the stair hall (room-9) are still stubs in this copy; re-run `$MCD room` after the merge to confirm the door-to-stove path.
Only one chair: the table is a two-cell run at the south end and the lane must stay clear, so there is no seat on the lane side; a second seat would need a different table placement.
The room view was rendered from above only (`rooms --out`); no separate inside eye view was made.
elements.md's I-house item (beds upstairs plus stoves x26 z12 and x33 z12) is only partly done here: the x33 z12 stove is built, the rest belongs to other parts, so I did not tick it.
plan.md has no per-room checkbox to tick, so the tick step was skipped.

waste.what: Worked out the layout cell by cell by hand: which of the 2 columns (x32 lane, x33 furniture) each z row takes, and that a table along x across the 2-wide room would seal the lane.
waste.cost: about 6 layout drafts in my head before writing the rows; no tool run for alternatives
waste.tool: A `room` or `plan` option that takes a furniture spec (object at x,z, kind) and reports lane/walk results before writing, so layouts get tested without a make.sh run each time.

waste.what: Table and chair placed by hand in layers() rows, because table_set only runs along x and a 2-wide room needs the table along z.
waste.cost: 2 layers() calls and 1 hand-typed fence/slab pair; a retry on the row widths (I first wrote 1-char rows)
waste.tool: vocab helper table_set with an axis option (along z), or a chair helper that picks facing from the table side, so the seat faces the table and its back lands on a wall.

waste.what: Working out the light by hand before running the check, to see whether one lantern could reach the far corner.
waste.cost: about 3 Manhattan-distance calculations; the check then confirmed min 10
waste.tool: `$MCD room` lantern spots printed before the first build, or a dry-run light mode that scores a lantern cell before placement.

waste.what: Walk verdict can't confirm a dead-end room from the entrance while the house front is still a stub; I had to reason the lane is open from the grid.
waste.cost: one extra make.sh-and-room cycle to see the same UNREACHABLE; no way to test the door-to-stove path in isolation
waste.tool: `mcd walk --from <room doorway>` (start the flood at a doorway cell instead of the street entrance) so each room can be checked before its neighbours are built.

companions.task: Design the table and chair, with a second seat if the lane allows, so the dining set reads as a set and not one chair at a corner.
Check the lantern plan against the room's real shape (2 wide, 6 deep), and say whether the stove's own light could carry the room without a hanging lantern.
Confirm the stair hall's flight and the doorway at x31 z11 are open to the lane, since the walk verdict depends on them.
